findings.title: Materials' 62-point lens gap is extreme
findings.body: Materials trades at a 62-point percentile gap between trailing and forward lenses, the widest in the table. The market is pricing 114 percent earnings growth next year, a bet that a cyclical trough is about to reverse hard.

findings.title: Energy's forward multiple hides earnings collapse
findings.body: Energy's forward P/E sits at percentile 38 while its trailing multiple is at percentile 84, a 45-point gap. That implies analysts expect 64 percent earnings growth, but the market is not paying up for it—the forward percentile is barely mid-range.

findings.title: Health Care at richest forward percentile ever
findings.body: Health Care's forward P/E is at the 100th percentile of its five-year range, yet its trailing multiple is only at the 87th. The market is underwriting 87 percent earnings growth, a level of optimism that has no precedent in this sector's recent history.
